title: The Story of the Lost Son
bigIdea: No matter what we have done, God runs to welcome us home.

memoryVerse.text: This son of mine was lost, and is found!

moral.lesson: God is like the loving father in this story. Even when we make bad choices and wander far away, God never stops watching for us. The moment we turn back to Him and say sorry, He runs to welcome us with open arms and forgives us completely.
moral.application: When you do something wrong, you don't have to hide or feel afraid. You can always come back to God and say sorry — and He will be so happy that you came home.

style: Flat-color children's cartoon storybook illustration, simple rounded shapes, soft warm colors, thick clean black outlines, bright and friendly, gentle lighting, 16:9 landscape composition, no text or words in the image, no letters.

characters.son: the younger son: a teenage boy with short dark hair and no beard, wearing a plain tan tunic
characters.father: the father: a kind older man with grey hair and a grey beard, wearing a warm red-brown robe

beats.scene: A kind grey-haired father stands outside a nice home handing a small bag of gold coins to his eager teenage son. The son looks excited to leave. Warm sunny day, gentle hills behind them.
text: Jesus told a story about a father who had two sons. The family had a good home and lived happily together.
But one day the younger son said, “Father, I don't want to wait. Give me my share of the money now.”
So the father gave him his share. Soon the young son packed up everything and traveled far, far away from home.

beats.scene: The teenage son, all alone in a far-away city, happily spending his coins at a lively party with food and other young people he just met. Coins are flying out of his bag. His father is NOT here — he is far from home.
text: In the faraway land, the young son spent his money on parties, fancy food, and foolish things.
He had lots of fun for a little while, and lots of people wanted to be his friend.
But he wasn't careful at all. Before long, every last coin was gone.

beats.scene: The teenage son, now ragged and sad and hungry, sitting all alone on the ground feeding pigs in a muddy pen. His tunic is dirty and torn. Grey, gloomy sky. He is completely alone — no one else is with him.
text: Now the young son had nothing left. He was so hungry that he took a job feeding pigs.
All his party friends were gone, and no one would help him.
Then he had an idea: “Even the workers at my father's house have plenty of food! I will go home, say I am sorry, and ask to be one of his workers.”

beats.scene: The grey-bearded father runs joyfully down a path with open arms toward his tired, dirty teenage son who is walking home. The father's robe flows as he runs. Warm golden light, happy and emotional.
text: So the son began the long walk home. He was nervous — would his father even want him back?
But while the son was still far down the road, his father saw him coming. His heart was filled with love.
The father didn't wait. He ran to his son, threw his arms around him, and hugged him tight!

beats.scene: A joyful welcome-home celebration outside the family home. The father puts a fine robe and ring on the smiling teenage son. Happy family and a table of food. Everyone is celebrating, warm and bright.
text: “I'm so sorry,” said the son. But the father was already calling for a celebration! He gave his son a fine robe and a ring — treating him like a son again, not a servant.
“My son was lost, and now he is found!” the father said with joy.
God loves us just like that father. No matter what we have done, He runs to welcome us home.
